prod._comment_domain: seqtek.com cutover deferred to Phase 6 — prod stays on CloudFront-default URL pre-cutover. Flip domainName + hostedZoneId together at Phase 6.
prod._comment_oidc: prod owns the account-wide GitHub OIDC provider; staging imports it. If the two envs ever move to SEPARATE accounts, set this true on BOTH.
prod._comment_ecr: staging creates the shared seqtek-website repo in this account; prod imports it. In SEPARATE accounts set this true on BOTH.

staging._comment_domain: seqtek-preview.com registered 2026-05-27 (T029a). Hosted zone auto-created by Route 53; CDK provisions ACM cert via DNS validation + A records on next SeqtekStagingEdge deploy. certificateSans/dnsRecordNames set to exactly what the old hardcoded [domainName, www.domainName] behavior produced — this env's already-deployed cert/records are unchanged by the certificateSans/dnsRecordNames split.
staging._comment_sizing: Validation-period free-tier-eligible sizes per Clarifications Session 2026-05-26. Flip to t3.small / db.t3.small / 50GB at Phase 5.5 launch-readiness review.

preview._comment_domain: Account [REDACTED_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID] — NOT a fresh/dedicated account (corrected 2026-08-10 after initial deploy attempt hit the account's 5-VPC-per-region limit): it already runs other real infrastructure (an 'intranet-sequred' ECS/FusionAuth/wiki stack, an RDS 'warehouse' database, and WordPress/SEO-hosting security groups under the Seqtek name in the SeqtekDeploy VPC). Cert covers seqtek.com + *.seqtek.com (reusable for any future subdomain with zero re-validation), but dnsRecordNames creates ONLY preview.seqtek.com — the zone's existing seqtek.com (A -> 89.106.200.1) and www.seqtek.com (CNAME -> client.gushwork.net) records are untouched. Hosted zone ZDNRI358EUS3R confirmed to already live in this same account.
preview._comment_sizing: Mirrors staging's validation-period free-tier-eligible sizing — this is a testing environment, not launch-readiness scale.
preview._comment_existingVpc: Account was already at its 5-VPC/5-IGW-per-region limit, and this VPC (SeqtekDeploy, pre-existing, unrelated to this codebase) is reused rather than requesting a quota increase. Its 3 existing subnets are all in us-east-1f only; ALB and RDS both independently require 2 AZs, so a new public+isolated subnet pair is added in us-east-1a (CIDRs 10.0.2.0/24, 10.0.40.0/26 — verified free against the VPC's existing 10.0.0.0/24, 10.0.1.0/24, 10.0.32.0/26 on 2026-08-10). The existing IGW is reused for the new public subnet's route; nothing existing in this VPC (its other subnets, route tables, default security group, or the WordPress/SEO/NFS security groups already there) is modified.
preview._comment_secondaryLane: TEMPORARY PROD-preview lane (added 2026-08-11, remove once seqtek.com cutover is ready): shares this env's cluster/ALB/RDS instance rather than standing up a whole separate env. Reachable at ww3.seqtek.com only — covered by the *.seqtek.com cert SAN above, zero new cert validation needed. New database 'seqtek_prod' on the SAME RDS instance, created by the lane's own container startup command, not a new rds.DatabaseInstance. seqtek.com and www.seqtek.com are NOT touched by this.
preview._comment_oidc: This env owns the account-wide OIDC provider (nothing else in this account uses GitHub OIDC). ownsAccountEcrRepository is FALSE despite that: the `seqtek-website` ECR repo already exists in this account (created + populated by hand during the first-deploy troubleshooting on 2026-08-10, when the ECS service's circuit-breaker rollback left it behind under ECR's default RETAIN removal policy) — CDK references it by name (ecr.Repository.fromRepositoryName) rather than trying to re-create it. Flip to true only after deleting that repo and starting clean.
